idiom_name: one hand-written transformation function per container type (no shared abstraction)
implementation_notes: C cannot state the operation at all: there are no generics over containers, no closures, and a value carries no runtime type information, so 'map for any context' has no signature - only per-payload-type functions (int_opt_map, str_res_map) or a type-erased void *(*)(void *) form that loses the payload type along with every compiler check. What remains is one concrete transformation per container, written where the container is already concrete, with the empty or failed branch repeated by hand in each of them. C11 _Generic can select a function name from the type of a controlling expression (the mechanism <tgmath.h> uses for its type-generic math macros), but it chooses between concrete functions per type - it cannot name the container abstraction or replace the function family. The classic form is never justified in C: the per-type function plus an explicit branch is the language-appropriate structure.
pitfalls: Every payload type needs its own function, so a codebase accumulates parallel map_* families that drift apart and must be kept in sync by hand.
The absent or failed branch is re-implemented per function; one early return that forgets the present flag silently turns a populated value into an empty one.
void * context pointers erase the element type: a single wrong cast inside a hand-written map is undefined behaviour the compiler cannot see.
_Generic selects one function per controlling type at compile time but cannot name the container abstraction, so it multiplies the function family instead of replacing it.
alternative: Write one concrete, type-specific transformation function per container (or fold the transformation into the loop that already walks the container). C has no way to express 'map for any context' without erasing the payload type; a struct plus a small family of named functions is the language-appropriate substitute, and where call sites genuinely need the shared abstraction, move that call site to a language that can state it.
